title: Beyond Gait: Validation of a brief neuropsychological battery for the tap test in normal-pressure hydrocephalus
summary:
Background: "Normal-pressure hydrocephalus" (often referred to as "water on the brain" in older adults) is a brain disorder characterized by an accumulation of excess cerebrospinal fluid in the brain's natural cavities. This typically leads to gait disturbances, memory problems, and urinary incontinence. A distinctive feature of this condition is that it can be curable in its early stages. To determine beforehand whether surgery (implanting an artificial tube to drain the fluid) would be beneficial, a "relief test" is performed in the hospital. During this procedure, a small amount of cerebrospinal fluid is withdrawn once via a needle in the patient's back. If walking or cognitive function improves following this procedure, surgery is considered a promising option. To date, doctors primarily assess improvements in walking after this test; changes in cognitive function and fine motor skills of the hands during the first two days post-test are rarely evaluated precisely or consistently in routine clinical practice.
Research Question: In this study, we aim to investigate whether a new combination of three brief, established tests - covering cognitive function and manual dexterity - is suitable for reliably measuring short-term improvements following the drainage of cerebrospinal fluid. We want to determine in how many patients cognitive function and hand function show measurable improvement, and whether there are cases where walking remains unchanged while cognitive function and hand dexterity improve significantly.
Methodology: This is a purely retrospective study. This means we are not testing new patients but are instead analyzing existing medical records of individuals treated for this condition at our clinic between 2019 and 2025. We will examine the test results obtained by patients immediately prior to the fluid drainage and two days afterward. This data is analyzed in a completely anonymized form, so that no link to real names can be established.

interventions.name: The present study examines the diagnostic and prognostic significance of a neuropsychological test battery as part of a CSF drain test in patients with suspected normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH). The data was collected retrospectively using the electronic patient files of the University Hospital

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Included are the datasets of all patients who, between January 2019 and December 2025, underwent the complete diagnostic workup for NPH—including the CSF tap test and pre- and post-puncture gait analysis—at the Department of Neurology, Knappschaft Kliniken University Hospital Bochum. The start of the inclusion period (January 2019) marks the implementation—standardized and unchanged since that time—of the neuropsychological test battery to be validated (comprising the MoCA, EpiTrack, and Grooved Pegboard) into the department's routine clinical workflow.
